lines.text: Hi, grown-ups! Today we're learning how an opt-out works.
Say hello to Little Switch!
Hi! I've got two sides: on, and off!
You typed a little question in a little search box line,
And an answer hopped on top of it and said, "I'll save you time!"
That's neat, but what if I would rather read the page myself?
Well, there's a tiny tab marked "Web," way up on the highest shelf!
I've only got two sides, it isn't much to learn:
You push me down for off... ...so how'd I just return?
Default on! Default on!
It was there when you woke up, it'll be there when you're gone!
You can hide it, you can mute it, you can tuck it out of view,
But the switch is just a picture that somebody drew for you.
Default on!
Now, "opt-in" means somebody asks you, and you say, "Well, sure, why not."
And "opt-out" means that no one asked you, and you're hunting for the spot!
And "default" is the setting that they picked before you came,
And if you never touch it, friend, they'll say you picked the same.
Got that? Opt-in, opt-out, default. There'll be a test.
There's always a test.
Now your inbox got a helper, and it wants to help you too!
A lawsuit says it flipped itself last fall, while out of view.
And what's the company say?
That they didn't, and here's the door:
Just a menu, then a menu, then a menu, then one more!
Then the TV got an update in the middle of the night,
And a brand-new tile was waiting in the early morning light!
Can I delete it?
You can hide it!
Is that the same?
...Next verse!
I've only got two sides, it isn't much to learn:
You push me down for off... ...so how'd I just return?
Default on! Default on!
It was there when you woke up, it'll be there when you're gone!
You can hide it, you can mute it, you can tuck it out of view,
But the switch is just a picture that somebody drew for you.
Default on!
Pop quiz!
There's a blue ring in the chat app where you talk to Mom and Dad.
I'll uninstall it!
Nope!
I'll mute it, then?
That's not so bad!
Now your phone has got an update, and it asks you to "Continue."
Where's the "No"?
There isn't one! It turned back on for you!
In Australia, office software went up forty-five percent...
Was there one without the robot?
Only once you tried to leave!
Now the school's the place for learning, and the school picks what you learn,
So the school said, "No AI, please," and waited for its turn.
And the giant said, "We hear you! Here's a deal that's very fair:
Take the robot with your search, or else there's no search there!"
Correction, boys and girls! You can switch the chatbot off,
And you keep your search and everything!
And the answer box on top?
...That one's "deeply integrated."
What's that mean?
It means it stays.
Default on! Default on!
It was there when we woke up, it'll be there when we're gone!
We can hide it, we can mute it, we can tuck it out of view,
But the switch is just a picture that somebody drew for you!
Default on!
I've got two sides.
...Guess one of 'em was just for show.
And that's how an opt-out works! Join us next week, when we learn about...
Who asked for that?
Hey, who wrote this song, anyway?
An AI did. ...But somebody asked it to.

shots.cue: Before the audio starts (about 2 s of room tone, added in the edit)
shots.picture: Pre-roll card on cream paper: "A cartoon for grown-ups about tech settings." Plain sans, warm dark-brown ink, film layer on, no bubble letters and no characters, so it reads as a label rather than a title. Cut straight to S01's countdown
shots.how: pre-roll card on room tone, before the countdown

shots.picture: Film-leader countdown, then the title card "DEFAULT ON" in bubble letters on mustard. A small toggle under the title flips itself from OFF to ON
shots.how: pre-roll countdown, title on the first downbeat

shots.cue: "Hi, grown-ups! Today we're learning how an opt-out works." (regenerated)
shots.picture: Narrator on a stool by a chalkboard reading "TODAY: HOW AN OPT-OUT WORKS"
Pan right along the wall to a wall plate; Switch's eyes open
Switch waves, then demonstrates: toggle up, an "ON" label pops; toggle down, "OFF"
A big generic search box on a desk; letters type themselves

shots.cue: "And an answer hopped on top of it…"
shots.picture: An answer box with legs hops onto the list of links and sits on them, squashing them flat

shots.cue: V02 "That's neat, but what if I would rather read the page myself?"
shots.picture: Switch lifts a corner of the answer box and peeks at the squashed links
Switch climbs a wobbling ladder to a tiny tab labelled "Web" on a high shelf
Night-blue background, one spotlight; Switch alone on the wall, singing slowly
Switch pulls himself down to OFF, exhales, closes his eyes
The grey sleeve enters from frame left and flips him back up. Click from the real-switch recordings
Switch looks left and right; nobody's there
Bright mustard background; bubble-letter lyrics with a bouncing ball

shots.cue: "It was there when you woke up…"
shots.picture: Sunrise over a bed with the answer box on the pillow; cut to the empty room at night, the answer box still there, waving

shots.cue: "You can hide it, you can mute it…"
shots.picture: Three beats: a blanket thrown over it; a mute bar over its mouth; it's shut in a drawer that slides back open

shots.cue: "But the switch is just a picture…"
shots.picture: Switch peels off the wall and turns out to be a sticker. A pencil finishes drawing him back on
Switch, redrawn slightly crooked, echoes quietly
The grey hand doodles little ON switches in a margin, in time with the fill
Chalkboard: "OPT-IN." A cartoon kid is offered a cookie and nods

shots.cue: V05 "And 'opt-out' means that no one asked you…"
shots.picture: "OPT-OUT." The kid already has a cookie stuck to his hand and wanders a maze of menus looking for the exit

shots.cue: "And 'default' is the setting that they picked…"
shots.picture: "DEFAULT." The kid sits down to a plate already piled with broccoli
A rubber stamp slams "YOU CHOSE THIS" onto the plate

shots.cue: "Got that? Opt-in, opt-out, default. There'll be a test."
shots.picture: The Narrator taps the three words; a stack of test papers thuds onto the desk
Switch, half buried under the stack
An envelope with eyes reads over a cartoon person's shoulder

shots.cue: "A lawsuit says it flipped itself last fall…"
shots.picture: A calendar flips to an autumn page; while everyone looks away, a tiny switch in the inbox's corner flips ON. Caption, held through S28: "Alleged in a lawsuit. Google denies changing settings."
Switch knocks on a door marked "SETTINGS"

shots.cue: "That they didn't, and here's the door: / Just a menu, then a menu…" (replaced)
shots.picture: The door opens on a menu, which opens on a menu, which opens on another, zooming in each time. Fine print scrolls past too fast to read: "on or about October 10"

shots.cue: "Then the TV got an update in the middle of the night,"
shots.picture: A living room at night: a TV with a progress bar, the moon in the window
Sunrise. A new tile sits among generic tiles on the TV's home screen, and winks
Switch drags the tile toward a trash can
The trash can turns into a box labelled "HIDE"
Switch lifts the lid; the tile is inside, waving
The Narrator yanks down a pull-down screen; whip transition
S09–S10 staging with a dimmer spotlight; the grey hand is already waiting at the frame edge
The hand flips him up faster than before
S13–S15 layouts with new gags: the answer box in a lunchbox, the mute bar sliding off, a sleeping bag instead of a blanket

shots.cue: "But the switch is just a picture…"
shots.picture: The sticker reveal again; this time Switch peels himself off before anyone else can, and sighs
Switch echoes, more tired
Game-show set with flashing bulbs and a "POP QUIZ!" sign; Switch at a contestant podium with a buzzer

shots.cue: "There's a blue ring in the chat app…"
shots.picture: A generic chat thread with "Mom" and "Dad" bubbles; a plain glowing ring floats in and parks at the bottom
Wrong-answer honk, big red X

shots.cue: V13 "I'll mute it, then?" / "That's not so bad!"
shots.picture: Half-credit chime; the ring puts on earmuffs and stays put

shots.cue: "Now your phone has got an update…"
shots.picture: A phone screen with one enormous button, "Continue," and nothing else
Switch searches the phone's edges with a magnifying glass. Pull back to a row of phones: on some of them, a setting slides to ON by itself. Caption: "Some iPhones, iOS 18.3.2, March 2025"

shots.cue: "In Australia, office software went up forty-five percent…"
shots.picture: A map card of Australia; a price tag inflates like a balloon to "+45%". Caption: "Microsoft 365 Personal. Alleged by Australia's ACCC."

shots.cue: V15 "Was there one without the robot?" / "Only once you tried to leave!"
shots.picture: Switch walks toward a door marked "CANCEL"; a cheaper price tag peeks out from behind it, then the door slams

shots.cue: "Now the school's the place for learning…"
shots.picture: A one-room schoolhouse at dusk, slow pan, Rhodes-only
A teacher's desk with a polite handwritten note on it
A giant pinstriped cuff (not the grey sleeve) slides a contract across the desk

shots.cue: "Take the robot with your search, or else there's no search there!"
shots.picture: The contract has two boxes, "Search + AI" and "No search"
The film burns from the centre, the frame jitters, and the shot rewinds at speed to S50
The Narrator redubs with mouth shapes visibly out of sync; a "CORRECTION" slate. The contract now has a third box

shots.cue: V16 "And the answer box on top?"
shots.picture: Tilt up: the answer box is bolted to the top of the frame, unchanged through the rewind
The bolts tighten themselves; a small label plate reads "deeply integrated"

shots.cue: V17 "What's that mean?" / "It means it stays."
shots.picture: Switch looks up at the Narrator; the Narrator looks away

shots.cue: Final chorus, through the second-to-last line
shots.picture: A classroom of cartoon kids, each with a little toggle on the desk; the toggles flick ON in rhythm. Bubble-letter lyrics with a bouncing ball. Switch in the front row, mouthing along
Pull back: the classroom is on the TV from S29, with the winking tile from S30
Switch alone on a black wall under a spotlight
He flips himself off three times and springs back on each time. On the third, the grey hand enters to flip him back…

shots.cue: "…Guess one of 'em was just for show."
shots.picture: …and stops mid-frame, hesitates, and withdraws. Switch is still ON, looking where it was

shots.cue: "And that's how an opt-out works! Join us next week…"
shots.picture: The Narrator wraps up; an end slate starts to slide in

shots.cue: [pop-up chime] / "Who asked for that?" ("Huh." isn't sung)
shots.picture: A "Summary of this song" box pops up over everything; its close button runs from the cursor
shots.how: chime in the gap; "Huh." is not sung

shots.cue: V19 "Hey, who wrote this song, anyway?"
shots.picture: Switch shoves the summary box out of frame
Film layer drops to zero. Real screen capture of the generation screen: style prompt, lyrics, take list
Split frame. Left: the generation screen. Right: the editing timeline with the Switch track labelled "Switch: recorded at home," its waveform playing

shots.cue: V21 "Hey… was its switch on, too?" over the band's last bars, then the audio ends (the band plays to the end of the file; there is no silence after the last word)
shots.picture: Real close-up of a light switch on a plain wall. On V21, a small hand reaches in and waits; on the band's last note it flips the switch OFF. It stays off. Hold two seconds on room tone after the audio ends, then cut to fact card G
shots.how: V21 over the band's tail; the hand flips on the last note; holds past the audio
shots.note: real footage; the shot runs past the audio (hold two seconds on room tone, then black)
